cases.translation: “She has come to stay with me,” said Princess Márya. “The count and countess will be here in a few days. The countess is in a dreadful state; but it was necessary for Natásha herself to see a doctor. They insisted on her coming with me.”

cases.sentence: — Вы знаете, что это было в тот ___, как нас освободили.
cases.explain: «самый день» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, is there a family free from sorrow now?” said Pierre, addressing Natásha. “You know it happened the very day we were rescued. I saw him. What a delightful boy he was!”

cases.explain: «прелестный мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, is there a family free from sorrow now?” said Pierre, addressing Natásha. “You know it happened the very day we were rescued. I saw him. What a delightful boy he was!”

cases.explain: «истинная правда» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes, that is really true,” Pierre hastily interrupted her.

cases.sentence: Пьер поспешил отвернуться от нее и обратился опять к княжне Марье с вопросом о ___ жизни своего друга.
cases.explain: «последних днях» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Natásha had already opened her mouth to speak but suddenly stopped. Pierre hurriedly turned away from her and again addressed Princess Márya, asking about his friend’s last days. Pierre’s confusion had now almost vanished, but at the same time he felt that his freedom had also completely gone. He felt that there was now a judge of his every word and action whose judgment mattered more to him than that of all the rest of the world. As he spoke now he was considering what impression his words would make on Natásha. He did not purposely say things to please her, but whatever he was saying he regarded from her standpoint.

cases.sentence: — Смущение Пьера теперь почти исчезло; но вместе с тем он чувствовал, что исчезла вся его ___.

cases.sentence: — Да, это было счастье, — сказала она тихим ___; — для меня наверное это было счастье.
cases.explain: «грудным голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes, that was happiness,” she then said in her quiet voice with its deep chest notes. “For me it certainly was happiness.” She paused. “And he … he … he said he was wishing for it at the very moment I entered the room. …” Natásha’s voice broke. She blushed, pressed her clasped hands on her knees, and then controlling herself with an evident effort lifted her head and began to speak rapidly.

cases.sentence: Княжна, сморщившись от желания удержать слезы, сидела подле Наташи и слушала в первый раз историю этих ___ любви своего брата с Наташей.
cases.explain: «последних дней» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Princess Márya, frowning in her effort to hold back her tears, sat beside Natásha, and heard for the first time the story of those last days of her brother’s and Natásha’s love.

cases.sentence: Она говорила, перемешивая ничтожнейшие подробности с ___, и, казалось, никогда не могла кончить.
cases.explain: «задушевнейшими тайнами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: She spoke, mingling most trifling details with the intimate secrets of her soul, and it seemed as if she could never finish. Several times she repeated the same thing twice.

cases.sentence: Лицо Николушки, похожее на отца, в минуту ___, в котором Пьер теперь находился, так на него подействовало, что он, поцеловав Николушку, поспешно встал и, достав платок, отошел к окну.
cases.explain: «душевного размягчения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At that moment of emotional tenderness Nikolúshka’s face, which resembled his father’s, affected Pierre so much that when he had kissed the boy he got up quickly, took out his handkerchief, and went to the window. He wished to take leave of Princess Márya, but she would not let him go.

cases.sentence: — Нет, мы с Наташей не спим иногда до ___; пожалуйста посидите.
cases.explain: «третьего часа» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “No, Natásha and I sometimes don’t go to sleep till after two, so please don’t go. I will order supper. Go downstairs, we will come immediately.”
